members.name: persuasion_v3
members.instructions: In a charity-donation chat, a persuader tries to get the other person (Persuadee) to donate to Save the Children. The input is the chat so far followed by the persuader message to tag. Tag ONLY the final persuader message (using the chat for context) with the single persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses. Judge by what the message does, not just its wording.

criteria.greeting: Opening or hello-type message: 'Hello', 'Hi there', 'How are you today?', 'Hello?' (even mid-chat). Greeting-exchange small talk at the start of the chat.
criteria.thank: Thanks for the persuadee's donation or help: 'Thank you so much for your donation!', 'Thanks so much!', 'Thank you, you are so kind!'
criteria.praise-user: A compliment aimed at the persuadee's character or choices: 'That is very generous', 'You are a wonderful person', 'I admire that'.
criteria.acknowledgement: Plain agreement or backchannel with no added content, or acknowledging a concern: 'Yes', 'I agree', 'Me too', 'It really is', 'Great!', 'I understand, that is a fair concern', 'Okay'.
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks specifically for a number/amount/percentage: 'How much would you like to give?', 'What amount are you willing to donate?', 'Say $500?', 'How about 20 cents?'. A message that only confirms an amount already agreed ('To confirm, you said 20 cents, correct?') is other.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: A direct yes/no ask or invitation to donate: 'Would you like to donate?', 'Would you donate some of your payment to Save the Children?', 'Would you take it?' after a pitch, 'You know you can donate a portion of your payment'.
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Minimizes the size of the request to ease the person into giving: 'Just a couple of dollars', 'Even 5 cents helps', 'Even a small donation makes a big difference', 'as little as $1 can feed a child', 'every penny counts', a few cents or dollars can have a huge impact, 'It is only the price of a coffee', 'Start small'. Emphasis is on how SMALL the amount is (small amounts still matter or cost you little).
criteria.donation-information: Mechanics of the donation task (statements, not requests): any amount from $0 to all of the payment (even 'from 0 to 2.00'), deducted from task payment, how and when money is sent, payment methods, website to donate, PayPal, matching programs. Not about the charity's merits, and NOT an ask: 'We are asking people today to give a small part of the payment' is proposition-of-donation.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Facts or claims about the organization itself: who they are, history, ratings, reach, what programs they run, how funds are spent (percent to programs), defending the organization against claims of scams or hidden finances with facts, results and lives saved by its programs, endorsements, what Save the Children does or is. Also general praise of the organization ('It is a great organization').
criteria.logical-appeal: Dispassionate reasoning or evidence about the effect/efficiency of donating: 'your donation will help children survive', 'you would not miss $1 but it matters to them', statistics about cost-effectiveness. Reasoning why donating makes sense.
criteria.emotion-appeal: Evokes sympathy or sadness: suffering, dying or vulnerable children, persuader's own sadness about it, asking the person to picture or think of the children, statistics/events about children harmed by violence or hunger ('1,000 children were killed in Syria'), 'children are our future'.
criteria.personal-story: A narrative episode with characters, events or a time span (a story about a child such as Bruce, something that happened to the persuader).
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader says they themselves donate or will donate, as an example: 'I give $30 a month', 'I donate to them regularly', 'I will donate 70% and you do 30%', 'I volunteer for them'.
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of the charity Save the Children, or what they know about it: 'Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'Do you want some info?'
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life, habits or experience: 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Do you volunteer?', 'Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?'
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinion, feelings or thoughts about the cause, the charity or children in general, or follow-up questions: 'What do you think?', 'How do you feel about child abuse?', 'What are you not sure about?', 'What is the best way to help the kids?'
criteria.off-task: Unrelated small talk or logistics of finishing the HIT: 'we need 10 chats to complete this hit', weather, unrelated topics.
criteria.other: Anything else: closings ('Take care, have a great day', 'Me too' to a goodbye), answers to side questions about the persuader ('I am well', 'I have a fridge full of food'), 'Do you have any questions?', neutral commentary, unintelligible.
